resources.string: Sagittal zones
Prostate zonal cutaway, with the front of the body at left.
Prostate base
The broad upper surface of the prostate meets the bladder neck, where the urethra enters the gland.
Prostatic urethra
This segment of the urethra passes through the prostate from the bladder neck to the apex.
Central zone
This wedge of glandular tissue surrounds the ejaculatory ducts. It is broad near the base and tapers toward the point where the ducts join the prostatic urethra.
Peripheral zone
This glandular region forms much of the back and sides of the prostate. In this section it faces the rectum and extends down toward the apex.
Prostate apex
The prostate narrows to its lower tip, where the urethra leaves the gland and continues toward the pelvic floor.
Sagittal cutaway
Vaginal canal in sagittal section, with the front of the body at left. The walls are shown slightly apart.
Posterior fornix
This recess lies between the back of the cervix and the upper vaginal wall. It reaches higher than the shallower recess in front of the cervix.
Anterior wall
The front wall of this fibromuscular canal lies behind the bladder base above and the urethra below.
Vaginal rugae
These transverse folds in the mucosal lining flatten as the vaginal wall stretches. The walls usually rest against each other along most of the canal.
Vaginal opening
The lower end of the vaginal canal opens into the vestibule, behind the separate opening of the urethra.
